thread:
sasha: Heads-up — we're seeing a spike of GPU pod preempts in ap-southeast-1 over the past hour. Pattern looks like pods are being spread across many nodes and then preempted when spot eviction happens.

sasha: Metrics: eviction count +420% on gpu-pool-small, tail latency for inference up 2.3x.

infra-bot: [ALERT] 1945678950 - node/gpu-node-ax3 high_pod_evictions (count=48) - cluster: prod-ap-southeast-1

leo: Is this the topologySpreadConstraint change we rolled last week? That made pods prefer spreading across AZs/nodes, right?

sasha: Yup. The rollout set spread weight to 100 in the new admission config to avoid co-locating heavy jobs. Seems to be backfiring with spot churn + small instance sizes.

maria: Also seeing a lot of cross-AZ egress from model shards when pods get scattered -> monthly egress estimate has jumped. Anyone quantified the cost impact yet?

devops: Quick datapoint: 2 hrs of this behavior ~ $4.8k in egress + 18% GPU idle inefficiency from fragmented allocations.

leo: We should prefer packing where possible for the dedicated/gpu-reserved tenants and keep spreading for best-effort/spot workloads. Can we make the spread constraint conditional on node label like node.kubernetes.io/gpu-pool=spot?

oncall: Agreed. temp mitigation: revert spread weight to 20 for gpu-pool-small and set a podTopologyConstraint override for label "redwood/high-bandwidth" so shard-y services stay co-located.

sasha: Proposed patch (kubectl):
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap admission-config -p '{"data":{"topologySpreadWeight":"20"}}'
```
Let's not do a full rollback, just tweak the pool-specific selector.

leo: Can we instead add a scheduler-plugin tweak — honor nodeAffinity for pods with annotation "redwood.co/pack-preference=prefer" with higher score? That keeps user-level config and avoids blanket changes.

maria: For short term, I want a label on affected deployments so cost team can tag them and run chargeback. Could we add an admission hook to inject redwood/cost-tag when pod lands on small pool?

devops: I can stand up the admission hook experiment. Will also flip autoscaler max surge to reduce churn.

oncall: Action items:
- devops: roll admission hook + autoscaler tweak to test on staging (ETA 2h)
- leo: draft scheduler-plugin change for selective packing (RFC by EOD)
- sasha: monitor evictions and egress after patch, post summary here (check at +1h)

sasha: Thanks — will keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: [NOTE] 1945679310 - runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-evictions - added correlation graphs.

maria: Ping me if costs still spike after the test, I'll open a billing incident.

leo: If the plugin looks hairy we can do a short-lived mutating webhook to flip pod topology constraints instead. Less infra risk.

sasha: Ok, will validate both approaches in staging.

oncall: Closing loop for now — moving to incident board if evictions > 500 in the next 3 hours.
